rules: INSPIRE Index Polygons is an open-source dataset developed for INSPIRE compliance.
The dataset contains locations of registered freehold property in England and Wales.
INSPIRE is a subset of HM Land Registry's wider Index Polygons database.
Files are divided by local-authority area.
A polygon crossing a local-authority boundary can appear in both authority files.
INSPIRE polygons show position and indicative extent, not definitive legal extent.
Each INSPIRE polygon has a unique Land Registry-INSPIRE ID.
The Land Registry-INSPIRE ID relates to a registered title.
The INSPIRE ID can be used with Find a Property to obtain registration and title-plan information.
The exact extent of land in a registered title cannot be established from INSPIRE polygons alone.
The individual title plan is required to identify registered-title extent.
A registered title has one title number but may contain several separate polygons.
Each separate polygon has its own Land Registry-INSPIRE ID.
Absence of an INSPIRE ID may mean land is unregistered, leasehold or another tenure excluded from INSPIRE.
HM Land Registry points users to the index map to check whether land is registered.
INSPIRE data is available for reuse under the Open Government Licence.
Use under the OGL is free.
Failure to comply with OGL conditions ends the granted reuse rights automatically.
Reuse requires HM Land Registry attribution.
Reuse of polygon geometry also requires Ordnance Survey attribution.
A link to the INSPIRE conditions should be provided where possible.
The dataset is updated on the first Sunday of each month.
Each monthly release represents data from the previous month.
The July 2026 download page states publication on 5 July 2026 and lists Barnet and Enfield.
HM Land Registry captures polygon geometry in British National Grid and warns BNG-to-WGS84 reprojection can shift some features by up to 15 metres.
Planning Data documents access to more than 100 planning and housing datasets.
Coordinate queries pass latitude and longitude to construct a point.
Coordinate queries return entities whose geometries intersect that point.
Multiple dataset parameters can be supplied in one coordinate query.
The q parameter supports postcode or UPRN search.
Planning Data states UPRN search is more precise than a coordinate for registered properties.
Entity results can include name, dataset, start-date, geometry and point fields.
Planning Data warns that an empty result does not prove no planning constraints exist because coverage varies.
The documentation example can fetch all 337 local planning authorities in one request.
geometry_entity can reuse an entity geometry for a spatial filter.
geometry_relation=within is documented for spatial filtering.
Raw geometry searches accept Well-Known Text.
WKT spatial-query coordinates should use WGS84 EPSG:4326.
geometry_relation supports within, equals, disjoint, intersects, touches, contains, covers, coveredby, overlaps and crosses.
offset is used to paginate large result sets.
The response links object includes next, prev, first and last pagination URLs.
Portfolio screening has no batch endpoint.
Planning Data recommends one request per property for API portfolio screening.
The field parameter can restrict returned fields.
exclude_field is subordinate to field when both are supplied.
The quality parameter can filter entity results by quality.
Planning Data recommends polite rate limiting for repeated property queries.
For large portfolios, bulk downloads plus local spatial intersections are recommended.
Bulk datasets are available in CSV and JSON and where applicable GeoJSON and Parquet.
The planning-application specification remains in development and local planning authorities are not currently required to publish applications to that specification.
The Environment Agency DTM 1m composite covers about 99 percent of England at 1m spatial resolution.
The DTM uses the last or only laser return.
Surface objects are removed using bespoke algorithms and manual editing.
The current composite was produced in 2022.
It combines Time Stamped archive and National LIDAR Programme surveys.
Where surveys overlap the newest best-resolution data is used.
Resampled data uses bilinear interpolation before merging.
The 2022 composite contains surveys from 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022.
Metadata index catalogues identify which survey contributed at a location.
DTM 1m downloads are GeoTIFF rasters.
Composite GeoTIFFs are supplied in 5km tiles aligned to the OS National Grid.
Elevation values are in metres relative to Ordnance Datum Newlyn.
The dataset uses the OSTN15 transformation method.
Individual source LIDAR surveys have vertical accuracy of plus or minus 15cm RMSE.
The DTM 1m record has no public access constraints beyond its stated licence.
The DTM 1m record uses the Open Government Licence.
The record states an annual update frequency.
The coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700.
The record exposes WMS, WCS, WMTS and OGC API service links.
Environment Agency guidance says WMS provides a summarised elevation view.
WCS provides raw pixel values such as elevation.
Persistent composite WCS endpoints remove the release-year suffix so clients can follow updates.
The supported WCS version is OGC WCS 2.0.1.
WCS GeoTIFF NoData pixels use the sentinel -3.4028235e+38 and must not be treated as elevations.
The WMS preview is only an image and cannot be queried for elevation values; downloaded composite ZIPs carry a GeoPackage index describing spatial location and temporal extent.
The current OS Data Hub page shows OS Terrain 50 Version Date July 2026.
OS Terrain 50 covers all of Great Britain.
The Data Hub lists ASCII Grid and GML for grid supply plus other contour formats.
OS Terrain 50 OpenData can be downloaded under the Open Government Licence.
OS Terrain 50 is an open height dataset and a digital terrain model.
The product is updated annually in July.
Grid and contour data are created from the same source data.
Grid and contour supplies use 10km by 10km tiles.
Tile identifiers use the National Grid reference of the south-west corner.
Terrain 50 grid points have regular 50m post spacing.
ASCII grid is a generic text-based DTM format readable by standard GIS software.
The supplied GML provides grid location, spacing and vertical-reference metadata for the ASCII data.
Each ASCII height value is calculated from the centre of its pixel.
ASCII rows run west to east.
Each grid row contains 200 pixels.
Each pixel is 50m by 50m.
Terrain 50 height values are given to the nearest 0.1m.
A grid tile supply includes ASC, GML, PRJ, ASC.AUX.XML and per-tile metadata XML files.
Terrain 50 metadata uses British National Grid EPSG:27700.
Terrain 50 metadata uses Ordnance Datum Newlyn EPSG:5701 for the vertical reference.
Per-tile metadata records flying dates and can store earliest and latest dates where a tile contains multiple surveys.
OS Downloads API lists OpenData products through GET /products and can return expanded product details.
A specific OpenData product is described through GET /products/{productId}.
OpenData download discovery supports fileName, format, subformat and area filters; TQ is a documented area value.
When redirect is requested and exactly one OpenData download matches, the Downloads API documents HTTP 307 redirection to the actual file.
